newsitem.title: USA: Fedex to use electronic logistics in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Fedex to use electronic logistics in Europe.

text.p: Federal Express Corp sees its move in the U.S. into the electronic logistics and commerce sector being followed by expansion into Europe, a senior executive told journalists Tuesday.
"We have high hopes of bringing our electronic commerce product to Europe very quickly -- within the next 12 months," senior vice-president for logistics, electronic commerce, Laurie Tucker said.
"For Europe our primary opportunity is helping our global customers gain entry to the European market. At the same time we feel we must conquer the U.S. first," she added.
"Electronically - with the Internet - it is very easy to expand and we've got quite a few plans for Europe. But we also need to make sure we first fully understand the market there," Tucker said.

Fedex sees this combination of its information technology expertise, time-definite package shipments, extensive route structure together with electronic ordering and delivery systems as a powerful competitive product.
"We are exploiting what we are good at ... there is no shortage of demand, customers are clamouring, demanding (the product), Tucker added.

This "virtual logistics" system enables manufacturers to ship directly to distributors or in some cases direct to personal customers bypassing traditional distribution chains, eliminating paper documentation and offering guaranteed delivery times, she said.

Tucker cited the case of an unnamed Fedex manufacturing client based in Austria, which then had its product packaged in the Netherlands, warehoused in Brussels and flown to Memphis for eventual distribution.

Simplification of the distribution chain has eliminated the Netherlands and Brussels. Eventually the product will be flown straight to the client from the manufacturer as and when needed on a time-definite basis.

"Our objective is to help customers eliminate inventory. It is to help customers move products more directly to their own customers," she said. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44-171-542-7706 Fax +44-171-542-5017
